sections.body: The X-wing is a stretch technique for harder 9 by 9 puzzles. It removes candidates when a number has exactly two possible places in each of two rows.
Suppose the number 7 can only go in column 3 or column 8 in row 2, and also only in column 3 or column 8 in row 6. The four squares form the corners of a rectangle, which is the 'X'.

Now reason it through. Row 2 needs one 7, either in column 3 or in column 8. Row 6 also needs one 7 in column 3 or 8. They cannot share a column, so if row 2 uses column 3, row 6 must use column 8, and the other way round.

Either way, one 7 ends up in column 3 and one in column 8. So no other square in column 3 or column 8 can be a 7. You can cross 7 out of every other square in those two columns. The same idea works with rows and columns swapped.
This is a logical proof, not a guess. If you cannot find an X-wing, ask for a hint in the game: it will point you toward a simpler step when one exists.
In a hard puzzle, write the notes for one number, such as 7. Look for two rows where that number has exactly two places, in the same two columns.
The X-wing is not needed for most puzzles. It is offered as a stretch for teens who enjoy logic. The key skill is the chain of reasoning: 'if this, then that, so either way this must be true'.

quiz.q: In rows 2 and 6, the number 7 can only go in columns 3 and 8. What can you eliminate?
options: 7 from every other square in columns 3 and 8
7 from every other square in rows 2 and 6 as well
Every number from every square in columns 3 and 8
hints: Think about where the two 7s must end up.
One 7 will be in column 3 and one in column 8, one from each row.

Example: if 4 can only go in rows 1 or 5 in column 2, and also only in rows 1 or 5 in column 6, the same idea works with rows and columns swapped: 4 is removed from other squares in rows 1 and 5. Decide which lines lose the 7 here.
quiz.explain: The two 7s fill columns 3 and 8, so no other square in those columns can be 7.

quiz.q: How many rows and how many columns are involved in an X-wing?
hints: The four corner squares of a rectangle make the 'X'.
A rectangle has two sides across and two sides up.
Example: a rectangle drawn on a grid has four corners, with two of them in one row and two in the next row. Count the rows and columns the corners use.
quiz.explain: Four corner squares sit in two rows and two columns.

quiz.q: In an X-wing, if row 2 puts its 7 in column 3, where must row 6 put its 7?
hints: Row 6 can only use column 3 or column 8 for its 7.
Two 7s cannot be in the same column.
Example: if two people can only sit in seat A or seat B, and one takes seat A, the other takes seat B. Use the same idea for columns.
quiz.explain: A column cannot hold two 7s. Column 3 is taken, so row 6's 7 must go in column 8.
